title: Counting 1–10, one-to-one
examples: How do I count these toys?
Can you show me how to count these blocks?
What does it mean to count one to ten?

explain.say: Let us count these apples together. We touch each apple as we say the number.
We touch the first apple, say one. We touch the second apple, say two. We keep going until we count all of them.
If we count all the fingers on your hands, we find the last number. That last number tells us the total count.

items: Say a number for every one

explain.say: Sometimes objects are not in a line. We still touch each one and say a number for every single object.

faq.q: If I count things in a line, do I have to touch them?
faq.a: Yes, it is best to touch each object as you count it. This helps you remember that you counted every single one.
asks: Do I tap when I count?

faq.q: What is the last number I say when I count to ten?
faq.a: The last number you say when you count to ten is ten. It means you counted ten things in total.
asks: What does the end number mean?
If I count to ten, what is the biggest number?

faq.q: If the objects are scattered, do I count them the same way?
faq.a: Yes, you count them the same way. You just make sure you touch every single object, no matter where it is placed.
asks: Does it matter if they are messy?
How do I count things that are not neat?

faq.q: If I count five things, what is the total number?
faq.a: If you count five things, the total number is five. You counted one, two, three, four, and five.
asks: What is the total when I count five?

faq.q: Can I count things that are not real objects?
faq.a: Yes, you can count things like shapes or pictures. You still touch or point to each one as you count.
asks: Can I count stars on the page?
Do I need real things to count?

facts: Counting helps us know how many of something we have.
When counting, we say the numbers in order, starting from one.
Touching each object as we count helps us count accurately.
The last number we say tells us the total amount counted.

quiz.say: Look at these three red balls. Count them.
quiz.why: You touched each ball one time and said a number for each one. So there are three.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you only looked at the first two balls.
wrong.1: This is tempting because you might have counted the space between the balls.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you only counted the first ball.

quiz.say: If you count your fingers on one hand, how many do you say?
quiz.why: You touched each finger one by one. When you finish, the total number is five.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might be thinking of something else.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you might count both hands at once.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might have stopped counting too early.

quiz.why: You must touch every single star, even if they are spread out. You counted six stars.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might have counted the space between the stars.
wrong.1: This is tempting because you might have counted too many times.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might have missed the last star on the right.
